beats.headline: Three kinds of summoning
beats.text: For the record: the subject's first note on file sits in the middle of the Cookbook's miscellaneous chapter. Avoid all three types of deity summoning. The big gods, Apito and Eris and so forth, are sponsored by some rich prick who paid extra to play the Celestial Ascendency, and they are invulnerable below the twelfth floor. Celestial boons, indentured summonings, involuntary summonings. In his short experience, all three lead to the summoner's death. Even the first. His advice: just stay the fuck away.

beats.headline: Gods as a revenue stream
beats.text: Below Crawler Forkith's reply, a second note by the subject covers involuntary summonings, which is what Crawler Carl's gauntlet did. They are common. God-summoning equipment is sprinkled through the dungeon as a way to collect more sponsorship money, allowing for special guest appearances, and the deity spots are often bought by celebrities. It is a safe way into the game for anyone not part of the dynastic families who control the armies of the ninth floor. Crawler Carl already knew most of it. He asks Mordecai anyway, so there is a record of the question.

beats.headline: A window with no glass
beats.text: Nineteenth edition, entry one of three. The subject went on a program tonight. They transported him to a ship floating in low orbit over his planet, with an open window that has no glass and is protected only by a forcefield. He calls it amazing. He can look down on his beautiful, lost planet. If he is to die here, he wants this to be his last view. Crawler Carl is at that moment about to be transferred to a sponsor's trailer, with the admin Loita, for a toy commercial.

beats.headline: Bugbear paste in his boots
beats.text: Entry two. Another program tonight. He has secreted bugbear paste into his boots and means to detonate them while in orbit. There are to be two admins on board. His Blast Shield skill should protect him from the explosion, if the skill works at all in that place; he does not know. If he blows the ship, it does not matter. Think of me, brothers, he writes. It is little, but it is all he has. Crawler Carl leaves robot Donut on the couch next to Loita and goes to do the commercial.

beats.headline: The admins were holos
beats.text: Entry three, and the last on file. He has blown the ship. His skill protected him, but the forcefield kept the ship from breaking apart, and the two admins who appeared to be with him were holograms. He was fooled, and he is ashamed. The gravity has failed, the temperature is dropping, and it is getting difficult to breathe. He does not think they can remove him while the forcefield holds. He can see his beloved Qurux. It shines and warms him in the cold. He prays someone avenges her, because he cannot.

beats.headline: Not god. Coolie.
beats.text: Robot Donut explodes in the green room. A massive crack runs across the picture window, and the blue forcefield is the only thing keeping the water out. It holds. Crawler Carl's first thought is to thank god, and his second corrects it: not god, Coolie. The admin Loita dies on the floor of that room, unable to teleport while the shield is up. Crawler Carl adds a note of his own to the Cookbook, addressed to the subject: he used this passage to plan the first step, and he did it for Coolie and for a little girl named Bonnie.

beats.headline: The source he protects
beats.text: Pressed to name his outside source, and offered a Legendary box for it, Crawler Carl does not give it up. If he names the Cookbook, it disappears. The version put to him, with polymers and technicolor residue reacting to space plastic, is more complicated than what happened. What he actually knew was simpler: the forcefield, thanks to the subject's passage, and that a disco ball covers everything in dust, from the same book. The rest was a toy panel he already knew was a piece of shit.

beats.headline: What Coolie would do
beats.text: In the saferoom, with the children watching The Last Unicorn and tens of thousands of NPC deaths planned for phase four, Crawler Carl thinks of the subject: the Cookbook author who sacrificed everything just in an attempt to kill two admins. He thinks of Priestly, too, and wonders what either would do in his position. His own answer: Coolie would do exactly what he is doing. Priestly would not.

beats.headline: His last view
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut are pulled onto a ship without warning, and the side wall is clear. Earth fills it: the Indian Ocean, the edge of Madagascar, mostly clear skies. Crawler Carl feels tears come, and thinks at once of the subject, who wrote the nineteenth edition. This was his last view, though of his own home planet. The file is now explicit: he died after a failed assassination attempt on a pair of admins. Crawler Donut vomits her tuna lunch.
